topical.text: Class I–II corticosteroid ± vitamin D analog (calcipotriene/calcitriol). Calcineurin inhibitor (tacrolimus, pimecrolimus) for face/intertriginous. Roflumilast 0.3% cream for sensitive sites.
topical.detail: Primary therapy for mild disease. Combination corticosteroid + vitamin D (Taclonex/Dovobet) improves efficacy over monotherapy. Reassess at 4–8 weeks. Taper steroid frequency to avoid atrophy.

photo-oral.text: Not typically indicated for mild disease.

biologic.text: Not indicated unless special site with significant DLQI impact.

topical.text: Class I steroid combo ± calcipotriene. Scalp: steroid solution/foam + clobetasol shampoo. Coal tar adjunct. Topicals continue as adjunct during systemic therapy.
topical.detail: Topicals bridge to systemic therapy and treat residual localized plaques. Maximize topical regimen 4–8 weeks before escalating.

photo-oral.text: Consider NB-UVB or an appropriate systemic therapy after assessing extent, difficult sites and impact. For U.S. Neoral plaque-psoriasis dosing, start 2.5 mg/kg/day divided twice daily; the labeled maximum is 4 mg/kg/day, not a universal 5 mg/kg/day.
photo-oral.detail: NB-UVB is first-choice phototherapy — safe in pregnancy, no systemic exposure. Methotrexate preferred systemic for concurrent PsA. Apremilast offers a favorable safety profile with no lab monitoring. Cyclosporine for rapid clearance needed.

biologic.text: Biologic eligibility depends on disease impact, comorbidities, prior treatment, preference and access; failure of ≥2 conventional therapies is not a universal clinical requirement.
biologic.detail: Distinguish payer access rules from evidence-based clinical selection.

topical.text: Adjunctive only — continue as maintenance on treated areas and for scalp/nail involvement.

photo-oral.text: Consider as bridge if biologic access delayed. Methotrexate or cyclosporine short-term. NB-UVB less practical for very widespread disease.
photo-oral.detail: Conventional systemics may be used as a bridge while awaiting biologic authorization. Cyclosporine provides rapid clearance for severe flares. Biologics are strongly preferred for sustained remission in severe disease.

biologic.text: IL-23 p19 inhibitors preferred for plaque psoriasis (guselkumab, risankizumab, tildrakizumab) — highest PASI 90/100 durability. IL-17 inhibitors (secukinumab, ixekizumab, bimekizumab) if concurrent PsA or rapid clearance needed. TNF-α inhibitors if comorbid IBD (adalimumab, infliximab, certolizumab).
biologic.detail: Target PASI 90 or DLQI 0–1 as treatment goals. IL-23 inhibitors offer once-quarterly dosing after induction and superior long-term clearance. Bimekizumab (IL-17A/F) has highest published PASI 90 rates at 16 weeks. Reassess response at 12–16 weeks; switch within or across class if inadequate response (PASI <50 at 16 weeks).

topical.text: Low-potency corticosteroids (hydrocortisone, desonide) in limited amounts. Emollients liberally. Avoid class I steroids over large BSA. Avoid tazarotene (teratogenic). Calcipotriene — limited data; use cautiously.
topical.detail: Topicals are preferred throughout pregnancy. Some psoriasis improves during pregnancy (immune shift). Minimize systemic absorption by using topicals sparingly and avoiding occlusion over large areas.

photo-oral.text: NB-UVB is an option in pregnancy. Avoid methotrexate, acitretin and tazarotene because of embryo-fetal risk. Use current narrative labels rather than obsolete FDA pregnancy letter categories; other systemic choices require specialist risk–benefit assessment.
photo-oral.detail: NB-UVB is the safest second-line option in pregnancy. All other conventional systemics are either contraindicated or have insufficient safety data. Apremilast has limited pregnancy data — avoid.

biologic.text: Certolizumab pegol (Cimzia) PREFERRED — PEGylated, Fc-free design minimizes placental transfer; classified low risk in pregnancy and breastfeeding. TNF inhibitors generally: low placental transfer in 1st and 2nd trimester; consider stopping adalimumab/etanercept in 3rd trimester to avoid neonatal immunosuppression. AVOID IL-17 and IL-23 inhibitors (insufficient pregnancy safety data).
biologic.detail: Certolizumab has minimal placental transfer. For other agents, continuation and infant live-vaccine timing require drug-specific and jurisdiction-specific advice; do not use a universal six-month rule.

citations.quote: Menter A et al. Joint AAD-NPF guidelines of care for the management and treatment of psoriasis with biologics. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2019.
